title: Buzuku Meshari 1555: Roman-rite vernacular witness identity control
semantics: One incomplete mixed Albanian Roman-rite-related witness, chiefly translated according to a retrospective Vatican report. An undated handwritten note attributes a Latin source. No Latin exemplar comparison, distinct Roman source recension, normative state, complete missal, act-history station, ancestry edge, or independent translation version series is asserted.

versions.title: Gjon Buzuku, Meshari: surviving 1555 Albanian Roman-related liturgical compilation
versions.qualification: The national catalogue identifies a facsimile of the incomplete Vatican-held exemplar, with lost title leaf and other missing leaves represented by blanks. The closing statement is reported to date composition from 20 March 1554 to 5 January 1555; [1555] printing is catalogued from the afterword, while place and printer are unknown. The book mixes Mass, sacramental, biblical, devotional and catechetical material. Vatican News 2026 describes it as chiefly translated, with some original Albanian material. The BKSH record separately reports an undated handwritten Italian note attributing a Latin source; no Latin exemplar or textual relation has been directly compared. Priest use is retrospectively reported, but approval, operative jurisdiction, exact contents and relation to Latin exemplars are unverified. This witness does not establish a distinct Roman source recension or act-history station.

negative_findings: No direct Vatican Library item record or original images resolved in this pass.
No complete 1958 facsimile acquired; Torrossa offers a licensed PDF, and BnF lists a print holding.
National Library facsimile catalogue cannot fill missing leaves or certify entire 1555 book.
Handwritten Italian note calling the book translated from Latin has no demonstrated contemporary date or approval force.
Reported priest use does not establish formal authorization, specific jurisdiction, or a separate Roman recension.
TITUS preliminary transcription is derivative and does not establish full original extent, exact typography, or collation.
cold_review_questions: Does the Roman-rite identification in Chiaramonte and the mixed Mass contents justify a Western Roman identity-control candidate while independent Albanian translation history remains deferred?
Is a new historical vernacular witness coverage row preferable to placing a 1555 mixed book under modern original-source adaptations?
Can BAV item metadata or licensed facsimile establish the exact missing-leaf census and Mass-content extent without conflating later editions with the 1555 witness?
Does any contemporary act prove Albanian priestly use, approval or jurisdiction beyond retrospective reports?
Should the 1555 chronology coordinate denote reported composition completion only, with [1555] printing confined to the date note?

retained_evidence.role: geographic origin and book 9559 control; not a direct book record

rights_policy: Only project-created bibliographic metadata is proposed for tracking. Eight downloaded HTML pages remain scratch-only; licensed BAV facsimile and original images were not acquired. TITUS prohibits republication without permission. No reusable book text or image rights are asserted.
limits: The 1555 plotted date is reported composition completion; bracketed [1555] printing is a catalogue attribution based on the afterword, not an inspected title page.
BKSH item is a later facsimile of a damaged Vatican exemplar, with missing leaves represented by blanks; no physical completeness or exact Mass-content census is established.
Roman-rite owner is a bounded historical identity classification; no Byzantine Albanian Church ownership follows from Albania geography.
